definitions.explanation: A small, sweet citrus fruit with loose, easy-to-peel skin. The most common citrus fruit in Japan, associated with winter.

examples.japanese: こたつで{蜜柑|みかん}を{食|た}べる。
examples.english: I eat mandarins at the kotatsu.

examples.japanese: {今年|ことし}の{蜜柑|みかん}は{甘|あま}くておいしい。
examples.english: This year's mandarins are sweet and delicious.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}になると、{愛媛|えひめ}や{和歌山|わかやま}から{蜜柑|みかん}が{届|とど}く。
examples.english: When winter comes, mandarins arrive from Ehime and Wakayama.

notes:
USAGE:
Usually written in hiragana (みかん) or katakana (ミカン). The kanji {蜜柑|みかん} is rarely used in everyday contexts. A quintessential winter fruit in Japan, strongly associated with sitting around a kotatsu.

CULTURE:
Eating {蜜柑|みかん} at the こたつ (heated table) is an iconic image of Japanese winter family life. Major producing regions include {愛媛|えひめ}{県|けん} and {和歌山|わかやま}{県|けん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {蜜柑|みかん}の{皮|かわ} (mandarin peel)
- {蜜柑|みかん}{狩|が}り (mandarin picking)
- {温州|うんしゅう}{蜜柑|みかん} (satsuma mandarin)
